Messages.Author: Roger Carhult
Messages.Body:
Card text:

Weapon, Gun. 2R damage each strike. Only usable at long range. If the bearer
blocks an action, he or she may set the range for the first round of combat
to long; if he or she does so, skip the Determine Range step on the first
round, and bearer must strike with this weapon on the first round.

Message 12 in thread
Från:LSJ (vte...@white-wolf.com)
Ämne:Re: Sniper Rifle V.S. Drawing out the Beast
Nyhetsgrupper:rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
View this article only
Datum:2001-09-22 14:59:15 PST

Nystulc wrote:
> James Coupe wrote:
> >Card text says:
> >
> > "If the bearer blocks an action"
> >
> >After you have brought the card into play via DW, the bearer does not
> >block an action.
>
> He is in fact the bearer, and he does in fact block. Seems to me that he

He "did" in fact block. But he wasn't a bearer when he did.

Card text isn't "if bearer blocked an action...", it's "if bearer blocks an
action...". Present tense. He must be the bearer when he blocks.

> satisfies the requirements of playing the effect regardless of whether he
was
> the bearer when the block began..

What in the card's text states he must be bearer when he blocks? The
sentence "If the bearer blocks an action, he or she may set the range for
the first round of combat to long;" doesn't state he needs to be bearer when
he blocks IMO. To set range he needs to be ebarer. After playing Disguised
Weapon he IS in fact bearer. It's when you want to set the range that you
read card text of Sniper Rifle. You don't read it before that. At the time
you read card text (because you're using the card) he is the bearer. he
wasn't bearer when he blocked, but card text doesn't clearly state "needs ot
be bearer when blocking", by the time you set the range the bearer did
actually block the action and he is a bearer (now) and that is enough,
that's how I interpret the card text.

I understand the current ruling has interpreted "if bearer blocks an action"
to require the bearer to have been bearer when blocking too, but I don't
understand why this ruling was interpreted like that. It could just as well
be interpreted "if bearer blocks an action" to mean that "if minion is a
bearer when wanting to determine range, and blocked the action, then...".

How are people supposed to know that Sniper Rifle checks for bearer not when
it is used, but when minion blocked? I think the card text would need an
errata to reflect that.

Roger

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <9v5al0$d28pl$1...@ID-104455.news.dfncis.de>, Roger Carhult

<rogc...@student.luth.se> writes:
>I understand the current ruling has interpreted "if bearer blocks an action"
>to require the bearer to have been bearer when blocking too, but I don't
>understand why this ruling was interpreted like that.

Because it uses the word "blocks" not "blocked".

It requires the bearer to block an action. The minion was not the
bearer when they blocked the action, in the situation of a Disguised
Weapon style card.

By being in the present tense, the effect triggers when the block
actually occurs, but is used before range etc.

> In message <9v5al0$d28pl$1...@ID-104455.news.dfncis.de>, Roger Carhult

> >I understand the current ruling has interpreted "if bearer blocks an
action"

>

>
> It requires the bearer to block an action. The minion was not the
> bearer when they blocked the action, in the situation of a Disguised
> Weapon style card.

I understand it's interpreted like this, but I don't agree with it. "Bearer
blocks" to me means that the one having the Sniper Rifle must block, which
is true in my case, AND that s/he needs to have a SR to be bearer, which is
ALSO true in my case. Card doesn't state when you checkf or bearer, to me
you check for bearer when you read the taxt, and *by the time* you read the
text, you've already equipped it with DW and thus IS a bearer. He *did*
block and is in fact *still* blocking since combat is part of block so the
present tense is moot as a reason to make the interpretation that has been
done.

> By being in the present tense, the effect triggers when the block
> actually occurs, but is used before range etc.

What rule states that present tense triggers when the block actually occurs,
and does NOT actually refer to the moment when the card is being read/used?
I've always thought card text applies when you use/play them. So the present
tense refers to the current moment, and at that particular moment I happen
to have a bearer who did block. I understand the current ruling, but I think
card text sin't clear enough. You can only know the current ruling by asking
LSJ, not by simply reading card text (which is how it ideally should be).

Roger
